title: 11 SIU officers probe fatal shooting: [North York Mirror Edition]
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit is continuing to investigate the death of a man shot while being arrested by police Sunday in a footpath near Edwards Garden southwest of Lawrence Avenue and Leslie Street.
O'brien Christopher-Reid, 26, was rushed to Sunnybrook and Women's College Health Sciences Centre where he was pronounced dead.
A police officer was shot in the leg and was released from the same hospital after treatment.

The SIU, a civilian agency that investigates whenever there is a serous injury or death involving police, has assigned 11 investigators, including four forensic identification technicians to the case.
Police said they received a 911 call about a shirtless man with a large knife in the Don Mills Road and Lawrence Avenue area around 12:10 p.m.
A short time later, a second 911 call was received about a man with a large knife in Edwards Garden, police said.
At about 12:25 p.m., 33 Division officers found the man and were in the process of arresting him, when he and an officer were shot.
SIU spokesperson Kaia Werbus said Christopher-Reid was not armed with a gun.
"We'll be looking at how the officer was shot," she told The North York Mirror yesterday. "We will be conducting a thorough investigation and we will be taking whatever time needed to do that."
The majority of SIU cases close within a month.
The results of an autopsy performed on Christopher-Reid's body Monday were not released by the SIU. Werbus said autopsy results are "pertinent to our investigation."
She would not say how many shots were fired or how many bullets hit Christopher-Reid.
The SIU has designated six witness officers and three subject officers. Subject officers are the ones whose conducts appear to have caused the death under investigation.
Investigators have interviewed five of the six witness officers and a handful of civilian witnesses.
Werbus said the subject officers have not been interviewed.
"We don't know at this point if they will be interviewed," she said. "They are not compelled to come in for an interview the same way as witness officers are under the Police Services Act."
According to Werbus, investigators are focussing on locating and interviewing witnesses, and "are also in constant contact" with Christopher-Reid's family.
"They will be requesting certain notes from the Toronto Police Service and reviewing those. They will also be reviewing evidence from the scene."
Investigators want to speak to a man and a woman who were having their engagement photos taken in the area at the time of the incident, Werbus said.
"Every witness statement will be factored into the investigation."
Richard Malone frequents the footpath where the shooting occurred. "A lot of people use that pathway for a walk. I'm really shocked," he said while walking past yellow police tape with his wife.
Carina, who did not give her surname, was planning to have a picnic with friends, but turned back when she saw police activity.
"A lot of families come here on the weekends," she said. "I never thought of it as a dangerous place at all. There are always many people around. I'm just very surprised."
